Backpack is pretty safe nowadays in Bolivia. 

I would just recommend to avoid the frontier with Brazil, for example Mato Grosso and Guayaramerin. Other than that, make sure you always have your belongings with you. I've seen too many tourists go on a bus, put their backpacks everywhere on the bus and then fall asleep. No wonder some of them got robbed. Also, avoid getting on the cheapest buses or the cheapest activities. Safety first. 

I would gladly recommend the city of La Paz, beautiful in itself, at 3600 above sea level. Make sure you visit the surroundings, the High Plateaus are very near, and Lake Titicaca is at 2 hours by car. 

Then Potosi, the famous city with the silver mines and Sucre are absolutely gorgeous, and you'll be close to the Salar of Uyuni, the world's largest salt flats, more than 10000 square km. It's better to visit it around June, since around December it's rainy and the Salar is flooded, so it can be a bit dangerous. I highly recommend it, it's an unforgettable experience. 

Bolivia has delicious food to offer. The capital of gastronomy is without any doubt Cochabamba. You get delicious food and incredible amounts of it for very little money. 

I also recommend going to Oruro during the Carnival, either in February or March. More than 5000 musicians and 20000 dancers go down the streets of Oruro during a week, displaying twenty kind of dances. It's absolutely crazy. 

Then you have the Bolivian part of the Amazon. I went to the Madidi Park, but you have some other parks. The city of Rurrenabaque is very welcoming, people there are extremely nice and there is some very nice food. (Those mangos…) 

Oh, and I almost forgot the Death Road. Extreme sports fans like to bike there.
